requirements.statement: Each router shall replay the active double-buffered calendar bank as a sparse ordered event list of up to 128 entries per bank. Each entry is {slot[9:0], valid[0], in_port[2:0], out_port_mask[4:0], opcode[3:0]} packed to 23 bits, sorted by slot. Calendar ID is 2 bits and an epoch bit selects the bank; only the inactive bank is writable and activation occurs atomically at slot 0 after old-epoch retirement. Dispatch uses next-event match: when global slot counter equals entry.slot, the calendar path fires.
requirements.resolution_rationale: Sparse event list replaces dense 2×1024×13 SRAM. Measured allreduce m=1 max 49 entries/router, max_slot 951; depth 128 provides >2× margin. Total storage per router is 2 × 128 × 23 = 5,888 bits (−78% vs dense 26,624). JSON export is naturally sparse.

rejected_alternatives.reason: 0.031 area class wasted; density ≪1% of address space.
Insufficient margin over observed max 49 without schedule rewrite proof.

requirements.upstream_compliance: Implements REQ-F-001; resolves OPEN-1-001 with SparseCal.
acceptance_criteria: BFM replaying all valid sparse entries fires exactly at entry.slot with encoded ingress, mask, and opcode.
Active bank is never written; no mixed-epoch replay.
Total calendar storage per router is exactly 2 x 128 x 23 = 5,888 bits.
Loader rejects duplicate (router, slot) entries and out-of-range ports/masks.

requirements.statement: Calendar replay shall use event-owned zero-buffer forwarding on slot match, while BG and escape traffic use a dedicated credited XY-DOR class on non-matching cycles (soft priority). Calendar wins when a matching sparse event fires; BG uses idle/non-matching slots and never displaces a firing calendar event. Conservative hard 1-in-16 non-borrowable bound remains 328 cycles on 12-hop worst case; soft-priority occupancy-aware bound is approximately 160 cycles.
requirements.resolution_rationale: Soft priority exploits sparse calendar occupancy (max 49 events over ~952 cycles) for better BG progress than hard TDM while preserving deterministic calendar replay.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Over-reserves BG slots given sparse occupancy; relaxed in Trial 3 with conservative bound retained.

rejected_alternatives.candidate: dedicated calendar VC with strict priority

acceptance_criteria: Mixed legal-calendar/BG BFM observes no cyclic wait; BG routes X before Y.
BG never grants over a firing calendar event at the same cycle.
Conservative 12-hop bound (|dx|=5, |dy|=7) ≤ 328 cycles under hard-TDM premises.
Soft-prio occupancy-aware 12-hop bound ≤ 160 cycles under max-occupancy-49 premise.

requirements.statement: Calendar payloads shall have no queued VC storage. BG/escape payload buffering shall use five per-input FIFOs of 20 flits each (100 flits, 51,200 bits per interior router), while per-egress credit counters enforce 16 flits horizontal and 20 flits vertical.
requirements.resolution_rationale: Static calendars need no payload queues; RTT-sized BG storage sustains full-rate under H=7/V=9.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Breaks vertical credit RTT full-rate progress.
Deferred to Trial 3b; out of scope for Trial 3.

acceptance_criteria: Credit counters never allow occupancy beyond allocated capacity.
Continuously granted H or V direction sustains one 512-bit flit per cycle after fill.
No legal backpressure test loses or duplicates a non-multicast flit.

requirements.statement: Trial 3 shall implement DCA Tier A only: reduce = calendar gather + PE-local compute; allreduce = gather + PE-local compute + calendar broadcast. The router shall not instantiate combine_unit or any DCA datapath/interface. CAL_OP_PE_HANDOFF may tag PE handoff but performs no router arithmetic. Tiers B and C remain comparison-only.
requirements.resolution_rationale: USER_CONFIRMED area-first feedback forbids in-router reduction; unchanged from Trial 2.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Rejected by binding feedback despite better small-m allreduce latency.

requirements.upstream_compliance: Satisfies A/B/C comparison mandate while selecting Tier A.
acceptance_criteria: Router RefC/BFM builds contain no combine_unit in the router datapath.
Reduce/allreduce calendar replays complete via gather/forward (+ PE handoff tags) without router arithmetic results.
No DCA transaction interface is active or required for base-router operation.

requirements.statement: The router shall use a 32-cycle calendar watchdog after expected arrival and immediate early/wrong-port detection. A violation releases its calendar reservation exactly once, preserves the flit plus remaining 5-bit leaf mask, and emits one credited XY escape packet per unserved destination; recovery starts within two cycles when queue capacity is available.
requirements.resolution_rationale: No-drop graceful degradation for off-calendar arrivals.
acceptance_criteria: Each violation class triggers exactly one reservation release.
Every remaining multicast leaf is delivered via escape/BG without loss.
Demotion action starts within 2 cycles once vc_buffers capacity exists.

requirements.statement: Analytic relative router area for Arch-A3 shall be 1.000× (or lower) versus IQ-XY baseline and strictly below Trial 2's 1.028×, using the audited component model in ppa-analytic.md with sparse calendar 0.009 and control 0.188.
requirements.resolution_rationale: Trial 3 sparse-calendar area target: IQ-XY parity via −0.031 calendar SRAM and +0.003 match control.

acceptance_criteria: ppa-analytic.md reports Arch-A3 total area 1.000 or lower.
Component sum equals crossbar+buffers+sparse_calendar+multicast+0 combine+control.
